- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.10) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.20), model tends to underestimate; increase forecast slightly.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 78.5), model often overcorrects downward; cap downward revisions to avoid excessive lag.
- Model frequently overestimates mean-reversion targets; if recent 5-day average is below 76.0, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overshoots late-period (last 5 days) prices; apply a 1–2% downward adjustment to final 5–7 days.
- If sentiment swings sharply (e.g., +0.30 to -0.30 in 3 days), model reacts too slowly; adjust forecast to align with sentiment direction within 2–3 days.
